Tap the mic once (or say your wake phrase) and Nonea listens again after every reply. Works only while the app is open. Hold-to-talk always sends a single message.

Android can’t reliably tell which language you’ll speak before you speak. Nonea starts with the language you used last, switches after a turn it recognises as the other one, and retries once in the other language if nothing matched. On Android 13+ some speech engines also detect it themselves.
Offline recognition needs the language pack downloaded in your phone’s speech settings and can be less accurate. “Offline only” needs Android 12 or newer.

This is not a true always-listening wake word. While Nonea is open on screen she keeps your phone’s speech recogniser running and reacts when it hears your phrase. It stops when you leave the app or lock the screen, uses more battery, may play your phone’s listening sound again and again, and, depending on your speech service, may send audio to Google while it listens. Off by default.

Nonea can press Back/Home, scroll, tap buttons by name and type into a text box, but only if you turn on Accessibility access in Android Settings AND switch automation on here. Both are off by default.

Android lets an accessibility service see what is on your screen and act on it. Nonea uses this only when you ask her to: to press Back/Home, scroll, tap a button you name, or type text you give her. Nonea reads the screen on your phone only to find the button; screen contents are never sent to Gemini or anywhere else. She never fills in passwords, never acts inside banking, payment, password-manager, Settings or install screens, never taps ads, and asks you before anything that could spend money, send something, delete, install or sign in. Android may also block her in some apps. You can turn this off any time.
I understand and want to continue
Switch it on yourself under Installed apps / Downloaded apps → Nonea AI.

Needs Accessibility access to be on and the explanation above to be accepted.
How to turn on Accessibility access

1. Tap “Open Accessibility settings” below.
2. Open “Installed apps” (or “Downloaded apps” / “Installed services”) and choose Nonea AI.
3. Switch it on and read Android's prompt.
4. Come back here. The status above should show it running. Then switch “Allow screen automation” on.
The red Stop button appears on top of other apps while Nonea is working, and “Emergency stop” here or in Phone tools cancels everything.
If the switch is greyed out (Android 13 and newer, for apps installed outside the Play Store): open your phone\'s Settings → Apps → Nonea AI → ⋮ menu → “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.

• Type into password fields, or act inside banking, wallet, password-manager, Settings and installer screens.
• Get around lock screens, fingerprint/face prompts, or any app that blocks automation.
• Act on apps that hide their screen from Android. When something can't be done, she tells you why and suggests doing it yourself or another way.
